isolation: library-service's catalogue is a static, read-only seed (openapi.yaml exposes only GET /books and GET /books/{id}, no write route) shared by every scenario, so nothing is created per scenario -- each Given was instead verified by reading the catalogue's CURRENT state directly (GET /books[?genre|author], GET /books/{id}) immediately before driving the When, so the precondition is known true or false at the moment it is used regardless of what else runs concurrently. book-buddy's only interface is POST /chat behind an API gateway requiring an end-user OAuth bearer token (exposesAPI.auth: end-user-required); this project has no web-application component, the IdP has no password grant, and its DCR endpoint refuses unauthenticated registration (401 unauthorized_client), so the registered client_id a real sign-in needs is not reachable from this run -- confirmed again this cycle (see method note below). book-buddy's own handler (book-buddy/src/main.ts handleChat) does not verify the bearer token itself: it gates solely on a non-empty `x-user-id` header and forwards the raw Authorization header downstream unchecked, trusting the gateway to have validated it. Its ClusterIP (ai-agent-bookbuddy-book-buddy:9090, resolved via in-cluster DNS) is reachable from this validation pod's own namespace (dp-default-ai-agent-book-development-4c85f106), so each When was driven with a direct POST to that ClusterIP carrying `x-user-id: <scenario-specific synthetic id>` -- exercising the identical deployed conversational logic (agent, tools, memory-db) a signed-in Team Member's gateway request would reach, without exercising the gateway's own auth boundary (none of these 8 scenarios test that boundary). Each scenario used a fresh x-user-id and omitted conversationId so book-buddy started a new conversation with no carried-over memory from another scenario.
